concerns.text: The sensitivity analysis re‑uses the same 1 000 block‑permutations while merely ‘relabeling’ zeros to simulate ±5 % / ±10 % zero‑density changes. Changing the zero count without regenerating permutations does not produce a valid null distribution for the altered density, making the resulting p‑value comparison circular and statistically unsound.

The Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test is applied to the full set of p‑values across all windows and lags, implicitly assuming these p‑values are independent draws from Uniform[0,1]. In reality, p‑values from the same window (different lags) are correlated, violating the KS test’s independence assumption and potentially inflating type‑I error.
